description: Bicep storage account whose network rules default to Allow
note: CIS Azure 4.7 and 4.8. Bicep now has two sources, not one. KICS parses .bicep natively where Trivy has no Bicep scanner at all, so this case's self-check compares two tools and the single-source caveat multi-iac-spec §4 carried for Bicep is retired. This case previously expected one rule where its ARM twin expected three, because 4.8 was reachable only through Trivy and Trivy has no Bicep scanner. KICS covers 4.8 on both, so the asymmetry is gone. CORRECTED after the confirming run: KICS's Trusted Microsoft Services query was expected here for the 4.8 half and does not fire, for exactly the reason checkov's CKV_AZURE_36 does not -- both gate it on defaultAction being Deny, and with Allow there is nothing to bypass. Two independent tools agreeing on that makes it the rule rather than a quirk. 4.8 is exercised by the insecure-transfer cases instead, where the account declares no networkAcls at all.
